# Lusa v2.0.0 — cross-compiled bare metal, verified in Renode

## Impact Introduction

Lusa could already emit freestanding `#[no_std]` C and place code and data in
linker sections, but turning that output into a bootable image still meant
hand-written startup assembly, a linker script, architecture flags, and an
emulator command line assembled by hand. That made bare-metal work hard to
reproduce and impossible to test in CI.

v2.0.0 makes hardware a first-class build target. `lusalang build --target
riscv32-virt` (or `riscv64-virt`) now drives a GNU RISC-V cross compiler,
links the embedded reset stub and linker script, and writes a freestanding ELF
image. The repository ships Renode platform descriptions and monitor
templates, plus a UART example whose output is asserted byte-for-byte on both
32-bit and 64-bit RISC-V. Embedded developers get a repeatable emulator loop;
compiler contributors get hardware-emulation coverage without owning a board.

Host builds are unchanged: without `--target`, `lusalang build` still uses the
host C compiler and produces the same native executable as v1.9.0.

## Feature Highlights

- **Explicit targets:** `lusalang build --target <name>` accepts `host`,
  `native`, `riscv32-virt`, `riscv64-virt`, and the GNU triples
  `riscv32-unknown-elf`/`riscv64-unknown-elf`.
- **Freestanding RISC-V images:** cross builds require `#[no_std]` and
  `#[entry]`, rename the entry wrapper to `lusa_entry`, and compile with
  `-ffreestanding -fno-builtin -fno-stack-protector -mcmodel=medany`.
- **Embedded startup and linker assets:** `renode/startup_riscv.S` initializes
  the stack and BSS, calls the entry point, and parks; `renode/linker_riscv.ld`
  places the image at `0x80000000` and reserves a 64 KiB stack.
- **Renode platforms:** custom `virt` descriptions for `CPU.RiscV32`
  (`rv32imac`) and `CPU.RiscV64` (`rv64imac`), 128 MiB RAM, an NS16550 UART at
  `0x10000000`, a PLIC, and a CLINT.
- **Deterministic UART capture:** `.resc` templates load the ELF, attach a file
  backend to `uart0`, run one emulated second, and quit. No interactive Renode
  session is needed.
- **Runnable example:** `examples/baremetal_renode_uart.lusa` prints a
  38-byte banner one `u32` at a time without libc.
- **Hardware-emulation tests:** `tests/module24_renode.rs` checks the assets,
  the freestanding C shape, and both boot paths. Execution tests skip cleanly
  when the optional tools are absent.
- **Dedicated CI:** `.github/workflows/renode.yml` downloads Renode and xPack
  RISC-V GCC on Ubuntu and runs the real emulator suite.
- **Documentation:** `README.md`, `docs/LANGUAGE.md`, and `docs/ROADMAP.md`
  cover the target table, toolchain discovery, platform map, UART rules, and
  local test commands.

## How to Use

Install a GNU RISC-V compiler (xPack `riscv-none-elf-gcc` 15.2.0 is the tested
toolchain) and put it on `PATH`, or set `LUSA_RISCV_CC`. Install Renode 1.17.0
or newer if you want to boot the image.

Create `hello_uart.lusa`:

```lusa
#[no_std]

-- Lusa has no u8 yet; Renode's NS16550 accepts 32-bit stores.
function uart_putc(byte: u32): void
    unsafe do
        local uart: *mut u32 = 0x10000000
        uart.write_volatile(byte)
    end
end

#[entry]
function _start(): void
    local message: [u32; 3] = [79, 75, 10]   -- "OK\n"

    local i: u32 = 0
    while i < 3 do
        uart_putc(message[i])
        i = i + 1
    end

    while true do
    end
end
```

Build it for either Renode machine:

```sh
lusalang build hello_uart.lusa --target riscv32-virt
# built hello_uart.elf for riscv32-virt with riscv-none-elf-gcc

lusalang build hello_uart.lusa --target riscv64-virt
# built hello_uart.elf for riscv64-virt with riscv-none-elf-gcc
```

The freestanding startup and linker script are embedded in the binary, so no
hand-written assembly is needed. The Renode platform descriptions and monitor
templates live in the repository's `renode/` directory. To boot the shipped
example from a repository checkout, render the monitor template and run Renode
headlessly:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/syntax-08/lusa
cd lusa
lusalang build examples/baremetal_renode_uart.lusa --target riscv32-virt

ROOT="$PWD"
sed -e "s|@PLATFORM@|@$ROOT/renode/lusa_riscv32_virt.repl|" \
    -e "s|@ELF@|@$ROOT/examples/baremetal_renode_uart.elf|" \
    -e "s|@UART_LOG@|$ROOT/uart.log|" \
    renode/lusa_riscv32_virt.resc > run.resc

renode --disable-gui --console --plain --hide-log run.resc
cat uart.log
# LUSA RENODE UART OK
# lusa virt v2.0.0
```

The platform and ELF replacements keep Renode's leading `@` file marker; the
UART log path is quoted plain text. Use a checkout path without spaces, or edit
the rendered `run.resc` paths manually.

To run the automated suite locally:

```sh
export LUSA_RISCV_CC=/path/to/riscv-none-elf-gcc
export LUSA_RENODE=/path/to/renode
cargo test --test module24_renode -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

Without those variables, the static tests still run and the execution tests
print a skip reason.

## Compatibility / Limits

- Cross-compilation requires an external GNU RISC-V toolchain; it is not
  bundled in the release archives. Host builds still use the existing
  GCC/Clang/TCC/MSVC discovery chain.
- Cross builds accept only `#[no_std]` programs with `#[entry]`. Hosted
  programs and no-entry freestanding programs fail before toolchain discovery.
- Lusa has no `u8` scalar. The UART example writes 32-bit values, which
  Renode's NS16550 model accepts. Real NS16550 hardware expects 8-bit accesses
  and THRE polling (line-status bit 5); use a board-specific driver on real
  silicon.
- The shipped platforms use a fixed `virt` memory map: RAM at `0x80000000`,
  UART at `0x10000000`, PLIC at `0x0C000000`, and CLINT at `0x02000000`.
  Interrupt-driven UART, clock configuration, and other boards are not covered
  yet.
- Renode and the RISC-V compiler are optional local dependencies. CI covers
  Linux x86_64; Windows and macOS users must install both tools to execute the
  boot tests.
- v1.9.0 is unchanged. Namespaced modules, async tasks, and all earlier
  language features keep their existing behavior on the host targets.

## Installation

Download `lusa-setup.zip` for Windows, or the matching
`lusa-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `lusa-linux-arm64.tar.gz`, or
`lusa-macos-arm64.tar.gz` archive. Unpack it and run `lusalang version` to
confirm `2.0.0`.

The release archives contain the host `lusalang` binary. To cross-compile,
install a GNU RISC-V toolchain separately and set `LUSA_RISCV_CC` or put
`riscv-none-elf-gcc` on `PATH`; install Renode separately to boot the emitted
ELF images.
